regions.name: Impact Ridge
regions.subtitle: Craters, ejecta, and signal clues
regions.question: Which observations connect a crater event to the ground and samples nearby?

observations.title: Crater rim and ejecta
observations.clue: Wide and close views show the rim, slope, and material around it.

observations.title: Before and after orbit images
observations.clue: Two dated images show a change that can be compared with the signal record.

observations.title: Candidate and local rock
observations.clue: Shape and measurements are clues, but appearance alone cannot identify origin.

branches.title: Rim overlook
branches.clue: Pin a wide view beside a close view to keep the landform context.

branches.title: Sample care station
branches.clue: Keep location and time beside the joined signal profile.

operations.title: Protected sample store
operations.benefit: Protected sample layout for later analysis.

operations.title: Accessible analysis rack
operations.benefit: Accessible sample layout for comparison during the shift.

regions.name: Wind Basin
regions.subtitle: Dust traces and equipment care
regions.question: What do dust traces reveal, and how can dust change equipment work?

observations.title: Sand around a blocker
observations.clue: Compare the sheltered and exposed sides of one rock.

observations.title: Clean and dusty equipment
observations.clue: A sensor window and a solar panel show different surface conditions.

observations.title: Dust at two scales
observations.clue: Local tracks and a broad image give different views of the same environment.

branches.title: Dune overlook
branches.clue: Mark the model inlet and outlet before running the dust path.

branches.title: Weather note
branches.clue: Compare a dust storm model with space-weather notes without mixing them.

operations.title: Clean solar panels
operations.benefit: Panels are clean and the post-shift record adds 2 EU.

operations.title: Treat recovered water
operations.benefit: Two recovered portions become two clean-water units after checks.

regions.name: Blackstone Steps
regions.subtitle: Cooled flows and layer order
regions.question: What can overlapping cooled flows tell us about relative formation order?

observations.title: Overlapping flow edge
observations.clue: Two angles show one cooled flow covering another.

observations.title: Cooled flow channel
observations.clue: A terrain view and a map sketch share the same channel shape.

observations.title: Local material comparison
observations.clue: A local rock can be compared with a reference without assigning an exact age.

branches.title: Flow-channel overlook
branches.clue: Highlight one covering edge to make the relation easier to read.

branches.title: Shelter cross-section
branches.clue: Open a cross-section that distinguishes insulation from shielding.

operations.title: Passive insulation
operations.benefit: Insulation panels help the work bay retain heat in the model.

operations.title: Supplemental heater
operations.benefit: A heater warms the sample bench quickly during the shift.

regions.name: Enclosed Ice Wall
regions.subtitle: Cores, labels, and clean water
regions.question: How can a core keep its context, and why is ice not automatically drinking water?

observations.title: Layered cover
observations.clue: Surface cover and a cross-section show a layered material record.

observations.title: Terrain and radar
observations.clue: The terrain profile matches a simplified radar section.

observations.title: Water ice and carbon-dioxide ice
observations.clue: Evidence, not color alone, distinguishes the two kinds of ice.

branches.title: Recovery-water station
branches.clue: Keep the Advance, Check, and Seal steps visible beside the water line.

branches.title: Food preparation note
branches.clue: Show why treated water and a labeled core follow different paths.

operations.title: Analyze the core
operations.benefit: Add a scanned layer and cross-section record to the core file.

operations.title: Treat recovered water
operations.benefit: Two recovered portions become two clean-water units after checks.

regions.name: Old Lake Shore
regions.subtitle: Context-rich rover records
regions.question: What belongs in an observation record before a clue can be studied further?

observations.title: Layered rock
observations.clue: Wide and close views show a useful geological relationship.

observations.title: Rover tool check
observations.clue: Camera, arm, wheels, and safe position are checked at the field target.

observations.title: Sample record
observations.clue: A location and witness-tube note preserve context around a sample.

branches.title: Dry-channel overlook
branches.clue: Use the channel direction to plan the next wide image.

branches.title: Context checklist
branches.clue: Keep wide image, close image, and position together in the record.

operations.title: Short transmission and rover check
operations.benefit: Send a checked summary and complete the rover inspection record.

operations.title: Full science transmission
operations.benefit: Send the complete image and context package for later review.
operations.deferred: Short transmission and rover inspection deferred.

intro: Touchdown confirmed. Take a look before you choose your first job.
Five stations. Where do we begin?
A place to explore—and a place to come back to.
dialogue.support: Support restores only the exact missing need. Your evidence stays safe.
dialogue.hold: HOLD names the missing base condition. Fix it, then send the proposal again.
dialogue.go: GO confirms the selected base can receive Leo and two Ares-1 crew for the first shift.
dialogue.arrival: Ares-1 has arrived. Leo can continue free exploration and practice.
